task: jepa.cpp inference timing and memory, tools/jepa-bench on synthetic deterministic input

protocol.ms: wall time of ggml_backend_graph_compute for the named graph (jepa_context_last_compute_ms); model load, graph build/alloc, host-side patchify and the output copy are excluded
protocol.wall_ms: the full public-API call, including all of the above
protocol.ms_mean/ms_min: over `repeat` measured runs after `warmup` unmeasured ones
protocol.encoder_ms: head/predictor rows only: the faster of two warm encoder passes that produced this row's input (a third, cold one runs first and is discarded)
protocol.tokens_per_s: tokens / ms_mean; for lewm-rollout ms is per step and tokens is 1, so the rate is steps/s
protocol.peak_rss_mib: process VmHWM after the run (weights + largest graph allocation)
protocol.ftype: the type requested at conversion time (the GGUF filename suffix)
protocol.ftype_gguf: what general.file_type says, which differs where a k-quant mix fell back
protocol.pytorch_ms: manifest timing_s.forward_s for the same frame count: mean over the samples, or the median of the samples after the first where the first is cold (>= 1.2 x the median of the rest); pytorch_basis says which was used for pytorch_speedup
protocol.pytorch_comparable: false where the reference forward is not the same work as our encoder (see the document's footnotes); no speedup is claimed
protocol.parity_ms: the same graph timed on the real fixture input in docs/parity.md
